docs.purpose: Lets a signed-in user request deletion of their own account. It marks the account and every subscription on it as pending deletion, schedules any active billing to stop at the end of the period they already paid for, and opens a 30-day window during which they can change their mind and reactivate.
docs.data_story: It reads 1 table — `user_profiles` and writes `user_profiles` and `entitlements`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. **Nothing in this repository calls it.** That is the state this registry exists to make visible, not a claim that it is dead — a caller could be a bookmark, an external system, or a path built from variables.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` is the field that matters most here: today it is empty, and the orphan panel renders that as a red row rather than leaving it to be discovered years later.

notes: Also cites docs/specs/02-web-admin/20_stripe_web_checkout.md §6. Idempotent — an already-deleted account returns a 200 no-op. Calls cancelAllStripeSubscriptions to schedule cancel_at_period_end on every live subscription; a Stripe failure is loud-non-fatal, logged and durably marked via stripe_cancel_failed_at for an operator sweep, never silently swallowed. A documented intentional gap: it does not force-revoke the user's already-issued session token, flagged in-comment for future security sign-off. NO in-repo caller — mobile/app/(app)/settings.tsx line 8 describes the intended POST in a comment only, and the surrounding code says Spec 97 §3 'will add' the Delete Account button; the route is built ahead of its UI. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: The Stripe cancel is LOUD-NON-FATAL by construction: it runs OUTSIDE the transaction (:67-96, after the commit at :65), and a Stripe failure is logged (:79) and durably marked in user_profiles.stripe_cancel_failed_at (:85-89) rather than failing the request — so a 200 does NOT prove billing stopped. A second, nested failure of the marker write is only logged (:93). Lines :98-125 are a long comment documenting a KNOWN GAP (no session/token revocation on delete) — that is a comment claim, not evidence of behaviour; the code contains no revocation call, which I verified by reading all 135 lines. CENSUS AGREEMENT: matches (reads user_profiles; writes user_profiles + entitlements). | Idempotency: GUARDED. A repeat call short-circuits at :45-47: if account_deleted_at is already set the route returns 200 { ok: true } without touching the DB or Stripe. The two DB writes share one transaction (:56-65). The Stripe side is separately idempotent: cancelAllStripeSubscriptions skips terminal statuses (src/lib/stripe/client.ts:157) and subscriptions already carrying cancel_at_period_end (src/lib/stripe/client.ts:158). | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control header, no revalidate/dynamic export (full file read :1-135) | ORPHAN — zero call sites in src/** or mobile/** (sweep 2026-09-15, comment lines stripped). | Locking tests: src/tests/user-profile-delete-stripe.infra.test.ts, src/tests/user-profiles.infra.test.ts.
